predecessors.name: Vakataka dynasty
predecessors.text: Telangana, the Vishnukundina heartland (the infobox area: "parts of present-day Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Odisha")

successors.name: Chalukyas of Badami
successors.text: Telangana with Guntur, Tenali and Ongole after the loss of Vengi

successors.name: Eastern Chalukyas
successors.text: coastal Andhra and Vengi, the lower Godavari-Krishna valley

ledger.x: 420: Madhava Varma I founds the Vishnukundina power.

c. 440: Madhava Varma II takes Guntur, Tenali and Ongole from the Ananda Gotrikas. "Madhava Varma II took Guntur, Tenali, and Ongole from [the Ananda Gotrikas], probably while they were subordinate to the Pallavas"; the page gives no year, and his reign is c. 440-460, so 440 (its start) is a bridge.

c. 440: Madhava Varma II conquers coastal Andhra and Vengi. "He conquered coastal Andhra and Vengi, moved the capital to Amarapura, and performed Vedic sacrifices"; the page gives no year, and puts the Vishnukundina reign "between the end of the Salankayanas and the rise of the Eastern Chalukyan power in 624", so the…

c. 616: Pulakeshin II and Kubja Vishnuvardhana take Vengi. "By about 616, Pulakeshin II and Kubja Vishnuvardhana took Vengi from the Vishnukundinas"; the Pulakeshin II page has Pulakeshin capture Pishtapura (undated; the Maruturu inscription puts it "around or before" 617-618) and make his brother governor of Vengi.

wars.name: Chalukya conquest of Vengi
wars.outcome: Pulakeshin II conquers the lower Godavari-Krishna valley and appoints Kubja Vishnuvardhana governor of Vengi; the Vishnukundinas end by 624.

wars.name: Vishnukundina-Pallava wars
wars.outcome: Madhava Varma II guarded against the Pallavas, and Vikramendra Varma II repulsed Simhavarman.

certainty.note: No frontier is given for any year; the extent follows the cities and districts named by the page (Telangana, Guntur, Tenali, Ongole, Vengi).
